formation.title: The Latin Empire
formation.text:
Constantinople has fallen, not to the infidel, but to the soldiers of the Cross. The greatest city in Christendom now belongs to the Latin lords who breached its ancient walls. Emperor and Doge, knight and merchant, must now decide what kind of empire will rise from the ashes of Byzantium.

The feudal lords of France, Flanders, and the Rhineland look to organize these conquered lands as they would any Western kingdom: fiefs parceled out, vassals bound by oath, the emperor supreme in war. But the Venetians who made this conquest possible demand their share: the harbors, the trade routes, the warehouses that made Constantinople the crossroads of the world.

Two visions compete for the soul of this new empire. Will it be a kingdom of knights, or an empire of merchants?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Rule as the Franks rule: by lance, by oath, by feudal law

modifiers.name: Frankish Feudal Order
modifiers.text: The Latin Empire has been organized along the lines of Western feudalism. Crusader lords hold their fiefs by military service, bound by the customs of France and Flanders. The emperor rules as first among equals, his authority resting on the strength of mounted knights and the loyalty of his vassals.

options.text: Embrace Venice: trade shall bind this empire together

modifiers.name: Venetian Partnership
modifiers.text: The Serene Republic has been embraced as the empire's indispensable partner. Venetian merchants control the harbors, the fleets, and the flow of goods through Constantinople. The Podesta sits at the emperor's council, and the golden thread of commerce binds the empire together more surely than any feudal oath.

advances.name: Partitio Romaniae
advances.text: The formal partition of the Byzantine Empire's territories among the Latin conquerors, establishing a feudal mosaic of crusader states across Greece and Thrace.

event.title: The Partitio Romaniae
event.text:
The conquered territories of Romania have been formally divided among the victors. By the terms of the partition treaty agreed before the walls were even breached, the emperor receives one quarter of all lands, Venice claims three-eighths (including the choicest harbors and islands) and the remaining three-eighths are distributed among the crusader barons as feudal fiefs.

The Duchy of Athens, the Principality of Achaea, the Kingdom of Thessalonica, and a constellation of island lordships now dot the map of Greece. Each lord rules his portion with the customs of his homeland, creating a mosaic of Western feudalism overlaid on ancient Greek soil.

options.text: The lands of Romania are ours to govern

modifiers.name: Romania Divided
modifiers.text: The territories of the old Roman Empire have been parceled out among the conquerors, each lord consolidating his hold over the Greek lands.

advances.name: Frankish Chivalry
advances.text: The heavy cavalry tradition of the French and Flemish crusader knights, whose devastating mounted charge decided battles from Adrianople to the Peloponnese.

advances.name: Latin Patriarchate
advances.text: The establishment of a Catholic patriarch in Constantinople, replacing the Orthodox hierarchy and asserting Roman ecclesiastical authority over the Greek churches.

advances.name: Feudal Levy System
advances.text: The obligation of every Latin vassal to provide armed men for the emperor's campaigns, binding the feudal lords of Romania to military service.

advances.name: Assizes of Romania
advances.text: The comprehensive feudal legal code governing the Latin lordships of Greece, codifying Western customs of land tenure, military service, and justice in an Eastern setting.

event.title: The Assizes of Romania
event.text:
A comprehensive legal code has been compiled to govern the feudal relations of the Latin lords in Greece. Drawing from the customs of Jerusalem, the laws of Champagne, and the practices of the Morea, the Assizes of Romania establish the rights and obligations of every vassal, from the humblest sergeant to the greatest baron.

The code addresses land tenure, military service, inheritance, and the administration of justice. It creates a common legal language for lords who came from every corner of Western Europe, binding them into a coherent feudal society despite their diverse origins.

options.text: Let the law of Romania be known to all

modifiers.name: Codified Law of Romania
modifiers.text: The Assizes of Romania have established a common legal framework across the Latin lordships, bringing order to the patchwork of Frankish, Venetian, and Byzantine legal traditions.

advances.name: Venetian Quarter
advances.text: The Venetian merchant quarter in Constantinople, a self-governing enclave where the commerce of East and West flows through Venetian warehouses and counting houses.

advances.name: Greek Silk Revival
advances.text:
The Latin lords recognized the value of the Byzantine silk industry and encouraged its continuation, blending Greek artisanship with access to Western markets.

Available in: Fondaco

advances.name: Pronoiar System
advances.text: The Latins adapted the Byzantine pronoia system, granting revenue-producing lands to mounted soldiers in exchange for military service, a hybrid of Western feudalism and Eastern administration.

advances.name: Archipelago Lordships
advances.text: The Duchy of the Archipelago and the scattered Latin lordships of the Aegean islands, where Venetian and Frankish lords rule from fortified castles overlooking the sea.

advances.name: Latin-Greek Synthesis
advances.text: Over generations, the Latin lords of Greece absorbed elements of Byzantine culture: the Greek language, Orthodox customs, and Eastern administrative practices blended with Western feudal traditions.

advances.name: Strait Control
advances.text: Control of the Bosphorus and Dardanelles straits, the narrow passages between Europe and Asia that command the flow of trade and armies between the Mediterranean and the Black Sea.

advances.name: Aegean Fleet
advances.text: A fleet of galleys adapted from the Byzantine dromon tradition, purpose-built for the island-dotted waters of the Aegean where speed and maneuverability matter more than heavy armament.

advances.name: Confessional Unity
advances.text: Efforts to bring the Greek Orthodox population into union with Rome, through persuasion, conversion, and the authority of the Latin Patriarchate.

advances.name: Bosphorus Arsenal
advances.text: A naval arsenal on the shores of the Bosphorus, drawing on centuries of Byzantine shipbuilding expertise to maintain the empire's fleet.

advances.name: Frankish Mercenary Tradition
advances.text: The Latin Empire's perpetual manpower shortage created a dependence on mercenary companies: Catalan, Aragonese, Italian, and French soldiers of fortune willing to fight for pay.

advances.name: Latin Administration
advances.text: The gradual development of a coherent administrative system blending Byzantine bureaucratic practices with Western feudal governance.

advances.name: Renewed Imperium
advances.text: The Latin Empire reasserts its claim as the legitimate successor to Rome, drawing prestige from its possession of Constantinople and the ancient imperial regalia.

advances.name: Mediterranean Arsenal
advances.text: The empire's naval capacity reaches new heights with the galleass, a heavy-gunned galley combining Venetian naval architecture with Byzantine seafaring expertise.

advances.name: Hellenistic Renaissance
advances.text: A cultural flowering as Latin scholars rediscover the Greek philosophical and scientific heritage preserved in Constantinople's libraries and monasteries.

advances.name: Balkan Consolidation
advances.text: The systematic integration of the Balkan territories into the imperial administration, replacing the patchwork of semi-independent lordships with direct governance.

advances.name: Constitutional Empire
advances.text: The evolution of the Latin Empire's governance into a constitutional framework, balancing imperial authority with the rights of the feudal lords and merchant communes.

advances.name: Eastern Modernization
advances.text:
The adoption of modern industrial and manufacturing techniques at the Bosphorus Arsenal, transforming it from a traditional shipyard into a naval supplies manufactory.

Available in: Bosphorus Arsenal

advances.name: Crossroads Hegemony
advances.text: The Latin Empire leverages its position at the crossroads of Europe and Asia to dominate Mediterranean commerce, controlling the flow of goods between East and West.

advances.name: Latin Legacy
advances.text: The enduring military traditions of the Latin Empire, a synthesis of Frankish heavy cavalry tactics, Byzantine defensive doctrine, and modern disciplined warfare.

destiny.name: Destiny of the Latin Empire
destiny.text: With Constantinople secured and the empire proclaimed, the Latin lords must now decide the shape of their destiny: whether by the sword or by the ledger.

event.title: Destiny of the Latin Empire
event.text:
The Latin Empire stands at a crossroads. Constantinople is ours, but the empire's future remains unwritten. Will the sons of the crusaders push ever eastward, as their fathers intended? Or will the merchant princes of Venice chart a course through commerce and control of the seas?

The choice we made at the empire's founding now bears fruit. Our destiny beckons.

destiny.name: Conquest of Greece
destiny.text: The crusader lords must bring all of Greece under the Latin banner. Athens, the jewel of antiquity, and Thessaloniki, gateway to Macedonia, must both submit to Frankish rule.

conditions.text: The Frankish feudal path has been chosen
Own Athína, or a subject owns it
Own Thessaloníki, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Conquest of Greece
event.text:
Athens and Thessaloniki fly the banner of the Latin Empire. The Duchy of Athens, once a prize fought over by Burgundian and Catalan adventurers, now answers to Constantinople. The Kingdom of Thessalonica, briefly held and quickly lost in the first years of the conquest, has been recovered and secured.

All of Greece, from the Peloponnese to Macedonia, acknowledges Latin overlordship. The crusader states are no longer isolated outposts. They form a coherent feudal realm.

options.text: Greece is ours. Now we look to greater conquests

destiny.name: The Anatolian March
destiny.text: With Greece secured, the Latin Empire turns its gaze across the straits. The ancient cities of Bursa and Konya (seats of Turkish power) must fall to extend the empire into Asia Minor.

conditions.text: Own Bursa, or a subject owns it
Own Konya, or a subject owns it

event.title: The March into Anatolia
event.text:
The banners of the Latin Empire now fly over the citadels of Bursa and Konya. What the Byzantine emperors struggled for centuries to hold, the Frankish knights have seized in a generation. The rich plains of Anatolia, once the heartland of Roman power, are open to Latin settlement and exploitation.

But the march has stretched our resources thin. Two approaches present themselves: press on with crusading zeal, or consolidate our gains with careful administration.

modifiers.name: Crusading Zeal
modifiers.text: The fervor of the holy war drives the Latin armies deeper into Anatolia, accepting economic disruption as the price of righteous conquest.

options.text: Consolidate: hold what we have taken

modifiers.name: Anatolian Consolidation
modifiers.text: A methodical approach to holding the conquered Anatolian territories, reducing military costs while building a sustainable garrison system.

destiny.name: The New Jerusalem
destiny.text: The ultimate crusader ambition: reclaim the Holy Land itself. Antioch and Jerusalem, lost prizes of the First Crusade, must be brought under Latin imperial protection. This is the culmination of two centuries of crusading.

conditions.text: Own Antioch, or a subject owns it
Own Jerusalem, or a subject owns it

event.title: The New Jerusalem
event.text:
The Cross stands triumphant over Antioch and Jerusalem. The dream that launched a thousand ships and sent a hundred thousand men into the wilderness of the East has been realized under the banner of the Latin Empire. The Holy Sepulchre itself is under our protection.

This is more than a military achievement: it is a vindication of the entire crusading ideal. The question now is whether this empire will be a holy kingdom consecrated to God, or a secular imperium in the Roman tradition.

modifiers.name: Holy Crusade Triumphant
modifiers.text: The recovery of the Holy Land has galvanized Christendom. Pilgrims and warriors flock to the Latin banner, inspired by the empire's sacred mission.

effects.name: Damage Done versus Heathens in Battle

options.text: A new Rome, heir to the Caesars

modifiers.name: Latin Imperium
modifiers.text: The Latin Empire styles itself as the true heir to Rome, a secular imperial power commanding respect through prestige, law, and diplomacy.

destiny.name: Aegean Dominion
destiny.text: The Venetian vision demands control of the sea lanes. Rhodes, where the Aegean opens on the Levant, and the great island of Crete must be secured to complete the chain of trading posts that the Duchy of Naxos began in the Cyclades.

conditions.text: The Venetian partnership path has been chosen
Own Ródos, or a subject owns it
Own Candia, or a subject owns it

event.title: Dominion of the Aegean
event.text:
Rhodes and the island of Crete now anchor the Venetian trading network in the Aegean. From Candia's great harbor to the walled port of Rhodes, Latin merchants control the sea lanes that connect Constantinople to the wider Mediterranean.

Every ship that passes through these waters pays tribute to the empire. The Aegean has become a Latin lake.

options.text: The sea is ours to command

destiny.name: The Silk Monopoly
destiny.text: Constantinople's silk trade was once the envy of the world. Restore the capital's market as the great emporium of luxury goods, where silk from the East flows through Latin hands to Western buyers, and build up Thebes, the silk town of Frankish Greece, whose looms once wove for the emperors.

children.text: Silk is produced in the market
Silk is traded in the market

conditions.text: We own Thebes and its development is at least 26

event.title: The Silk Monopoly
event.text:
Constantinople has reclaimed its ancient role as the world's greatest marketplace for luxury goods, and at Thebes the looms are busy again. Silk from China and Persia, spices from India, and furs from the north all flow through our markets, taxed and traded by Latin merchants.

The question before us is how to best exploit this windfall. We could invest in the production of finished goods, transforming raw silk into fine cloth. Or we could focus on customs revenues, taxing the flow of goods through our harbors.

options.text: Invest in our workshops and looms

modifiers.name: Constantinople Silk Exchange
modifiers.text: The empire's investment in silk production and processing has created a thriving luxury goods industry, though the focus on trade comes at a cost to naval readiness.

options.text: Tax the trade that flows through us

modifiers.name: Crossroads Customs
modifiers.text: A systematic customs regime taxes the immense flow of goods through Constantinople's harbors, funding ambitious construction projects across the empire.

destiny.name: The Eastern Emporium
destiny.text: Extend the trading network to its fullest reach. Kaffa on the Black Sea and Smyrna on the Aegean coast will anchor a commercial empire spanning two seas, backed by a treasury deep enough to finance it.

conditions.text: Own Kaffa, or a subject owns it
Own Smyrna, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Eastern Emporium
event.text:
From Kaffa on the Black Sea to Smyrna on the Aegean coast, the Latin Empire's trading network spans two seas and a dozen peoples. Our merchants trade in every port, our bankers finance every venture, our ships carry the goods of three continents.

We stand at the crossroads of the world. Shall we focus on the rich Levantine trade routes to the south, or turn northward to dominate the Black Sea and its hinterland?

modifiers.name: Levantine Trading Network
modifiers.text: A sprawling commercial network connecting the ports of the Levant to the markets of Europe, generating vast wealth but diverting resources from scholarly pursuits.

options.text: The Black Sea shall be our domain

modifiers.name: Black Sea Hegemony
modifiers.text: The Latin Empire dominates the Black Sea, controlling the flow of grain, furs, and slaves from the northern shores through its network of trading colonies.

units.name: Frankish Knight
units.text: Armored crusader knights from the heartlands of France and Flanders, whose devastating mounted charge carried the Fourth Crusade to the walls of Constantinople.

units.name: Pronoiar
units.text: Mounted soldiers granted pronoia estates in exchange for military service, blending the Byzantine land-grant tradition with Western knightly combat techniques.

units.name: Latin Dromon
units.text: A war galley descended from the Byzantine dromon tradition, adapted by Latin shipwrights for patrol and combat in the narrow waters of the Aegean and Bosphorus.

units.name: Latin Galleass
units.text: A heavy war galley mounting substantial artillery, combining Venetian hull design with Byzantine seafaring traditions to create a formidable vessel for eastern Mediterranean warfare.

buildings.name: Crusader Tower
buildings.text: A fortified tower house in the Frankish style, built to secure conquered territory and serve as the seat of a Latin lord.

buildings.name: Fondaco
buildings.text: A Venetian-style trading house combining warehouse, residence, and marketplace, where merchants from across the Mediterranean conduct their business.

buildings.name: Island Lordship
buildings.text: A fortified coastal estate on one of the Aegean islands, where a Latin lord commands both soldiers and sailors from his castle above the harbor.

buildings.name: Mercenary Hall
buildings.text: A gathering place and barracks for the Western mercenary companies that form a crucial supplement to the Latin Empire's limited feudal manpower.

buildings.name: Bosphorus Arsenal
buildings.text: A major naval shipyard on the shores of the Bosphorus, drawing on centuries of Byzantine and Venetian shipbuilding expertise.

buildings.name: Latin Academy
buildings.text: An institution of learning where Latin and Greek scholarship meet, preserving the intellectual heritage of both traditions.

buildings.name: Holy Sepulchre Commandery
buildings.text: A fortified religious-military commandery dedicated to the defense of the Holy Land, garrisoned by knights sworn to protect the sacred sites of Christendom.

buildings.name: Emporion
buildings.text: A grand trading entrepot where merchants from across the Mediterranean and beyond gather to buy, sell, and exchange goods under the protection of Latin law.

list.name: Partitio Romaniae
list.text: The treaty signed 1 October 1204 dividing the Byzantine Empire among the Fourth Crusade victors: three eighths to Venice, a quarter to Emperor Baldwin, and the remainder enfeoffed to crusader barons holding plena potestas in exchange for annual military service from June 1 to September 29. The partition entrenched a hereditary feudal aristocracy whose loyalty was contractual rather than personal, leaving the Latin throne structurally weak but its baronial host formidable.

list.name: Cour des Pairs
list.text: The Haute Cour, the feudal council of barons modeled on the curia regis of the Kingdom of Jerusalem. At Constantinople the emperor convened it with the Venetian Podesta and his six-member council; at Andravida, twelve Achaean baronies reduced their prince to a first among equals, forbidden to decree capital punishment without their consent. Its judgements formed the precedent base later codified in the Assises de Romanie.

list.name: Patriarchatus Latinus
list.text: The Latin Patriarchate established after the conquest of 13 April 1204, with the Venetian subdeacon Thomas Morosini consecrated as inaugural patriarch. It supplanted the Orthodox Ecumenical Patriarchate, imposed the Roman rite and unleavened bread on Byzantine churches, required new bishops to be consecrated by Latin forms, and conducted services in Latin rather than Greek, the theological lever for the Union of the Churches that was the Crusade's original ecclesiastical pretext.

list.name: Podesta Venetus
list.text: The Venetian Podesta of Constantinople, who governed the three eighths of the city north of the Mese assigned to Venice, used the Byzantine title despotes to assert near-equality with the emperor, and answered to the Doge rather than the Latin throne. Heading a six-member council and a separate slate of officials across the empire's ports, he was an ambassador and vicegerent more than a vassal, a role continued after 1265 by his successor the Bailo for centuries beyond the Palaeologan restoration.

list.name: Assises de Romanie
list.text: The legal code of the Frankokratia, compiled from the customs of the Principality of Achaea and the precedents of the Haute Cour. It drew on the Assises de Jerusalem and grafted Byzantine pronoia practice onto Frankish feudal procedure, governing paroikoi tenure, fief obligations, and the juridical position of the Greek population. Through Achaea its norms diffused to Cyprus and the Aegean islands as the canonical legal text of Latin Greece into the late fifteenth century.
